title: Adjusting to a Blunter Workplace Culture
script: Aisyah: [thoughtful] Can I be honest? I nearly cried in a meeting yesterday, and it wasn't even really about the criticism itself.
Mentor: I heard it was a fairly direct review. What specifically threw you off about how it was delivered?
Aisyah: [carefully] At my last company, feedback was always softened, cushioned with compliments first. Here, someone just said the report was disorganized, full stop.
Mentor: That bluntness can feel jarring at first, particularly if you're used to feedback being wrapped in reassurance before the actual point arrives.
Aisyah: [reflective] It felt personal, even though logically I know it probably wasn't meant that way at all.
Mentor: Here, directness is generally treated as a form of respect, believe it or not. It assumes you're capable of hearing something plainly without needing it softened.
Aisyah: [honestly] That's a generous interpretation. It could just as easily be a lack of consideration for how comments land on the receiving end.
Mentor: That's fair, and honestly, some people here do lean too far into bluntness without much tact. Not every direct comment is delivered thoughtfully.
Aisyah: [gently] So how do I tell the difference between genuinely useful directness and someone simply being careless with their words?
Mentor: Ask yourself whether the comment addressed the work specifically, or whether it characterized you as a person. Yesterday's comment, from what you've described, targeted the report, not you.
Aisyah: [calmly] When you separate it that way, it does land differently. I think I'd folded the two together without realizing it.
Mentor: Most people here would rather hear the blunt version early than a polite version too late to actually fix anything.
Aisyah: [encouraging] I suppose I've been treating politeness as proof that someone cares, when maybe directness here means exactly the same thing, just expressed differently.
Mentor: Precisely. Give it another month before deciding whether the culture suits you; first impressions of tone are notoriously unreliable.
Aisyah: [seriously] Alright. I'll try responding to the content next time instead of reacting to the delivery immediately.
Mentor: That single shift alone will probably change how comfortable you feel here far more than the culture itself will.

quiz.question: What upset Aisyah in the meeting?
options: Direct, unsoftened feedback that her report was disorganized
Being ignored completely
Losing a project
Being publicly praised incorrectly
quiz.explanation: Aisyah was upset by direct feedback saying the report was disorganized, with no softening or compliments first.

quiz.question: How does the mentor explain the workplace's directness?
options: As a sign of disrespect
As something unique to Aisyah's team
As a rule nobody actually follows
As generally being treated as a form of respect, assuming people can hear things plainly
quiz.explanation: The mentor explains directness here is generally treated as a form of respect, assuming people can handle plain feedback.

quiz.question: What does Aisyah push back on?
options: That feedback should never be given
That directness always means respect; it could just be a lack of consideration
That her report actually was well organized
That the mentor is wrong about everything
quiz.explanation: Aisyah points out that bluntness could also just reflect a lack of consideration for how comments land, not necessarily respect.

quiz.question: What test does the mentor suggest for judging feedback?
options: Whether it was said loudly
Whether it came from a manager
Whether it was written or spoken
Whether the comment addressed the work specifically or characterized her as a person
quiz.explanation: The mentor suggests checking whether the comment targeted the work itself or characterized her as a person.

quiz.question: What does Aisyah decide to try going forward?
options: Quit the job
Respond to the content of feedback rather than reacting to its delivery
Avoid all future feedback
Report her colleague to HR
quiz.explanation: Aisyah decides to try responding to the content next time instead of reacting to the delivery immediately.

quiz.question: Why did direct criticism of the report initially feel personal?
options: Correct orders, inform customers, and equip support staff.
The department's future hiring plan remained unsettled.
The employee came from a culture where feedback was softened first.
An employee says a colleague presented her idea without credit.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The employee came from a culture where feedback was softened first.

quiz.question: What limitation does the colleague admit about workplace bluntness?
options: Some direct comments lack tact and thoughtful delivery.
It recorded evidence, actions, ownership, and corrective commitments.
It included budget tasks, monthly feedback, and a review date.
Evidence is needed before confirming wrongdoing or assuming jealousy.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Some direct comments lack tact and thoughtful delivery.

quiz.question: How can the employee distinguish feedback from a personal attack?
options: Blame did not replace analysis of the system.
Both people would retain the same record of commitments.
Check whether it describes the work or the person's character.
Name the action and responsibility without defining the person's character.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Check whether it describes the work or the person's character.

quiz.question: Why do coworkers often prefer clear criticism delivered early?
options: The review had not turned her into the symbol of failure.
A fair review is due, but promotion is not guaranteed.
It leaves enough time to improve the work.
Document decisions, ideas, and owners while work is happening.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It leaves enough time to improve the work.

quiz.question: What period does the colleague suggest before judging the culture?
options: Ask why one ordinary error travelled so far undetected.
The narrator gained clear evidence targets and a decision date.
Recognition affects promotion, pay, and access to future assignments.
Observe it for another month before deciding whether it fits.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Observe it for another month before deciding whether it fits.
